references.text: Abraham shows hospitality by washing his guests' feet and giving them food, just as the old man does in Judges 19:21.
Lot shows hospitality to the angels by taking them into his house, corresponding to the actions of the old man.
Laban receives Abraham's servant, provides fodder for the camels and water to wash feet, reflecting Oriental hospitality.
Joseph's steward gives Joseph's brothers water to wash their feet and fodder for their donkeys, similar to the scene in Judges.
Jesus mentions the custom of washing guests' feet as a sign of hospitality.
Jesus washes the disciples' feet, referring to the ancient custom of footwashing as an act of hospitality.
Paul mentions footwashing as a virtue of a worthy widow, showing that this hospitality custom continued in the early church.
